intro: Suggesting a plan, agreeing on the time and place, and saying what you are going to do.
b1.titulo: Meeting up and the near future
b1.texto:
To suggest a plan, use **quedar**:

- **¿Quedamos el sábado?**
- **Quedamos a las seis en el café.**

And to talk about a plan in the near future, use **ir a + infinitivo**:

- **Voy a estudiar.** (it is not the present, it is what I will do)
- **¿Qué vas a hacer mañana?**

Note: the verb that changes is **ir** (voy, vas, va…); the other verb stays in the infinitive.
b2.f5.texto: What are you going to do tomorrow?
b4.texto:
The near future is formed with **ir** + **a** + infinitive:

- **Voy a estudiar** esta tarde.
- **Vas a venir** mañana.
- **Vamos a ver** una película.

It is the most natural way to talk about nearby plans. The future with -é («estudiaré») exists, but it sounds more formal.

And a very useful phrase for making an excuse: **Es que…** → «Es que trabajo».
b5.f0.texto: Lucía wants to meet up with Pablo on Saturday.
b5.f1.texto: She asks him if he can make it at six.
b5.f4.texto: They arrange to meet on Sunday morning.
b5.f5.texto: They are going to go to the cinema.
b5.f6.texto: Lucía is going to buy the tickets.
b5.f7.texto: Afterwards they are going to have something at the café.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The text does not say that; it says he works.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The text does not mention that.
b7.pregunta: Complete with the correct form of «ir».
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: «voy a estudiar» is the near future with «yo».
b7.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: «va» goes with él, ella or usted.
b8.traduccion: I am going to study tomorrow.
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «What are you going to do tomorrow?».
p.quedamos.consejo: «Quedar» also means to arrange to meet: «¿Quedamos el sábado?» suggests a plan.
p.a qué hora.glosa: asking the time of a meeting
p.a qué hora.consejo: «Qué» has an accent. The answer takes «a»: «a las seis».
p.el café.glosa: the place where you have coffee
p.el café.consejo: It can be the drink or the venue. «En el café» is the venue.
p.trabajar.consejo: The j sounds like a strong h: tra-ba-HAR.
p.mañana.consejo: The ñ sounds like «ny». Without «la», «mañana» is tomorrow; with «la», it is the first part of the day.
p.puedo.consejo: The o becomes ue: puedo, puedes, puede.
p.el cine.glosa: the place where you watch films
p.el cine.consejo: The c sounds like th in Spain: THI-ne.
p.el domingo.glosa: the last day of the week
p.el domingo.consejo: Days of the week are written in lowercase in Spanish: el domingo.
p.la entrada.glosa: the ticket to get into a place
p.la entrada.consejo: It is also the way in: «la entrada del edificio».
p.tarde.consejo: Here it is an adverb: «llegar tarde». Do not confuse it with «la tarde», a part of the day.
